chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Instrumentation and arrangements copied from records
summary: The six-piece band had no bass and made head arrangements from records of Coon-Sanders, Moten and Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let's go back to the -- you had six guys.
Well, let me see. Banjo, piano, drums, trumpet, alto and tenor.
No bass. The banjo, we just had the banjo.

Well, we listened to the records and we'd play like the records and then we'd make head arrangements. You know, whenever -- Malone was this teacher I told you about, he would write us some arrangements, so he had written us maybe like -- we had about 15 or 20 arrangements that he had written for the band. He could write, man. He could just -- fast and write and everything, but we couldn't. And a lot of things he had written, we couldn't play. It was a little too heavy, you know. We would take us a long time, like get our introduction --
You mean you took arrangements off records?
Yeah, we was listening to Fletcher. And McKinney's Cotton Pickers --
